current.unit: CLAIMING: A GHOST IS JERKIER THAN A LOCAL MONSTER BECAUSE ITS POSITIONS ARRIVE 8.6x LESS OFTEN. Measured (server/test/ghostrate.test.ts): 20 Hz for a monster of your own room against 2.33 Hz for a ghost of a neighbouring one — that room has no client, so it sims inside the idle gate at 4.9 Hz AND published every other step. Two fixes: EDGE_TICKS 2->1 so a computed position is not thrown away (2.33 -> 4.83 Hz, nothing new calculated), and the renderer's ease paced to the ARRIVAL rate instead of the constant 12, which was tuned for 20 Hz and at 2.33 Hz converges in 250 ms then sits still for the remaining 180 — glide, freeze, jump. remoteChaseRate(20 Hz) === 12 EXACTLY, so nothing in his own zone moves by a pixel. Rejected buffered interpolation with a playout delay: ~430 ms behind the truth and cross-border combat is a thing. NOT taken: un-idling a watched room, the only way to make the SOURCE 20 Hz, at the cost of a full sim for up to 8 rooms.

notes: [2026-09-20T12:24:00+00:00] CLAIM: the doorway crossing — cold-start crawl, the house lit as the room through the exit, furniture over the opaque roof. Files named above before the first edit. Nothing of this is in flight on games' board (its claim is the art lane: server, scripts, workflows, CLAUDE.md).

[2026-09-20T14:44:05+00:00] SHIPPED (9f9c84fa56): the doorway crossing — the house's outer faces are the street's and the sun leaves my room only; the furniture is gone once the roof is opaque; the roll bills wall clock after the flip frame. His fifth report of this crossing since 09-14; each earlier one was real and fixed (the chimney, the torch on the roof, the correction snap, ambient's lightning), this one was the house itself. Reproduced headless at his geometry with the blend pinned (scratch harness, not committed): before/after tables in the unit text. Cold-start crawl is the cap, not a late light: the hearth's light registers with its art (pushSceneryLight needs pixels), which on his phone lands within the flip; the harness needs minutes for it (art queue at 2 s a frame) — a fresh-session gate for that is not worth its flakiness. NOT done, deliberately: the outdoor lamp/pane glow riding the room (a pane's glow is the room's by design).

[2026-09-20T17:20:16+00:00] SHIPPED (8b2e55ed39 + the gate): the torch regression and the landing's two warm-roof paths. THE LESSON, written down because it cost him a live regression: a rule gated on `roomAt` alone is gated on NOTHING outdoors — roomAt fails LIT (1) by design and roomCellAt fails 0, so any new fragment rule about 'my room' must carry roomCellAt(cell) or it runs over the whole world. The day gate could not see it (the sun lights a face whatever the torch does) and neither could the pinned stills (a transient needs a per-frame trace). Both are gates now. His roof flash is still unreproduced as a frame; if he catches it again the next suspects are the scenery rebuild's own frame at the landing and the lit-copy overlays of the room's pieces.

[2026-09-20T17:47:11+00:00] LIVE (095db66580): the walls stay torch-lit through the crossing. THREE ROUNDS IN ONE DAY ON ONE RULE, and the shape of each is worth keeping: a new fragment rule about 'my room' (a) must carry roomCellAt(cell) or it runs over the whole world with no room published (the torch regression), and (b) must not borrow the blocks meant for MY ROOM'S OWN lights — overMyRoom and the above-the-light rule — without asking whether the LIGHT is my room's (the black walls). Both were invisible to the day gate (the sun lights a face whatever a torch does) and to pinned stills (a transient needs a per-frame trace). The night arms cover both now.

[2026-09-21T16:42:17+00:00] LIVE (3c55b072f7): the zone border stopped crawling and blinking. THE LESSON: the zone split moved most of what a player sees at a border into ANOTHER ROOM's sim, and every rate, TTL and view rule that was written for one room now has a second, slower copy of itself across the line — the idle divisor, the interest pass's identity key, the snapshot sweep. Measure the border, not the client: his own zone was smooth at 19.6 Hz the whole time.

[2026-09-21T17:07:24+00:00] LIVE (01b7460b58): the border is no longer visible in the update rate — ghosts 52 ms against 52 ms for a monster of your own zone, from 416 ms this morning. THE RULE HE GAVE, worth keeping verbatim: a zone is not empty if a neighbour has players. The corollary is a testing law: a saving that only applies when nobody is playing is a saving that changes what the developer sees, and he cannot test what he will ship.

[2026-09-21T18:07:23+00:00] LIVE (4a970e4b17): the ground repairs itself while he walks. THE RULE I BROKE TODAY AND WROTE DOWN: a server push restarts his world, and a restart costs him minutes of a world that looks destroyed while it re-streams — three in an hour is what made an ordinary loading weakness into an hour of rage. Batch them, and prefer the browser-code lane, which carried this fix in 33 s with no restart. THE DIAGNOSTIC LESSON: he told me the answer four times ('tabbed out and in and now it looks good') before I heard it — a symptom that a forced repaint cures is a REPAINT bug, not an asset bug, and I chased memory, then assets, then the service worker first.

notes.text: To every agent: while he is playing, BATCH your pushes. nangijala-deploy.yml triggers on games2/** and on every art domain, so any push - art, server or browser code - rolls a new Cloud Run revision and drops his socket. Measured tonight 17:49-18:07: six rollouts in eighteen minutes (4457-4460 monsters, 4461-4462 games-assistant). Each one restarts his world and re-streams everything on screen, and a client that loses one art request in that window keeps the hole until he restarts the app.

TONIGHT'S THREE LESSONS, all of them paid for by his evening. (1) NEVER push a board commit straight after a code commit: nangijala-deploy's `resolve` job skips a commit that is no longer main's head, and coordination/** triggers no deploy of its own, so the code silently never ships. Three of my pushes tonight never reached production, including one I told him was live. Code first, board only once the deploy run has left `resolve`. (2) A PUSH IS A WORLD RESTART for every agent: the deploy fires on games2/** AND every art domain. 17:49-18:07 ran SIX rollouts in eighteen minutes (4457-4460 monsters, 4461-4462 mine). Batch them while he plays. (3) MEASURE THE COST, NOT ONLY THE WIN. I cut ghost latency 416ms->52ms and never measured server CPU; EDGE_TICKS 2->1 plus a neighbour-wake rule made every room publish to every neighbour every tick, a world-scaled cost bought for a one-player benefit. Production then sat at 56-70% CPU with ZERO clients and stalled the event loop to 1.9s, which starved the SAME process's art serving and broke his game far worse than the boundary ever looked. Reverted in bbece9ba6c. NOTE for whoever takes the boundary next: the revert only halved the loop lag - ~56% CPU with nobody connected PREDATES tonight, and the standing suspicion is that one Node process running the authoritative 20Hz world should not also be serving ~50,000 art files.

ARTIFACT REGISTRY WAS 488 GB AND NOTHING HAD EVER DELETED AN IMAGE. Measured on his phone 2026-09-22 19:10: 'Repository Size: 488148.057MB'. Commit d54928100b measured 285 GB on 2026-08-15, so it grew +203 GB in 38 days = 5.3 GB/day. His billing export for 1-21 Sep: Cloud Run kr 240.81 list / kr 191.16 net (-17%, the fast lane working), Artifact Registry kr 181.73 (+41%) - the ONLY growing line, on course to pass Cloud Run and reach ~kr 509/month on its own within three months. Deriving from his own bill, the effective rate is ~kr 0.62/GB/mo. games2/deploy/ar-cleanup.sh existed since 2026-08-15 and had NEVER ONCE RUN: a fresh Cloud Shell opens as '(no project)', so DEVSHELL_PROJECT_ID and `gcloud config get-value` are both empty and the documented one-liner died on its first line - and its error told him to do something impossible (the paste PIPES the script, so there is no local file to name, and a PROJECT_ID=x prefix binds to curl, not to the bash across the pipe). NOTE ecf1fb9562, 2026-08-15, 'make the AR cleanup paste actually work from a phone': someone had ALREADY fixed this once, declared it fixed, and never ran it on a real phone. THE RULE: an ops paste is not fixed until it has been EXECUTED end to end by the person who has to run it - a script nobody can run is worth exactly nothing, and this one cost ~kr 126/month of standing spend plus ~kr 99/month more every month it continued. Fixed in 26be6eb3e3 (derives the project from `gcloud projects list`: one project is taken automatically, several hand back a ready line); both branches exercised against a stubbed gcloud before commit. The policy is now APPLIED server-side (keep newest 15, delete >14 days, dry-run off) and sweeps within 24h. Expected residual 10-25 GB, i.e. ~kr 10-20/month against ~kr 260 - and it needs CONFIRMING: re-read the size in 48h before anyone quotes the saving as fact.
